reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Sunday in late July has a particular texture. The week ahead hasn't started pulling at you yet. The lawn needs mowing or it doesn't. There's coffee, and light coming through the window at an angle you didn't notice when you were hungover on Sundays and just trying to survive until Monday.

When I was drinking, Sundays were a wasteland. Damage control. Trying to piece together what I'd said, who I owed an apology to, whether I could stomach food yet. The day existed to be endured. Now it's just — a day. And I used to think that sounded boring. Like sobriety was going to reduce my life to a series of quiet Sundays and nothing else. What I didn't understand is that the quiet Sunday is the ground everything else grows out of. The ski trips, the real friendships, the trip you actually remember — none of that exists without the boring Sunday underneath it. The boring Sunday is where you become someone your future self can trust.

Durant's line about Aristotle gets misread as being about greatness. It's not. It's about the accumulation of small, unglamorous choices. Today you make coffee. You call your mom back. You go for a walk. Nothing dramatic. And that, repeated, is the whole thing. That's how the life gets built.
reflection.meditation: Sit for a few minutes with the ordinariness of today. Nothing has to happen. You are already doing the work by being here, sober, on a Sunday morning.

affirmations: I am building a life on ordinary days, not just the big ones.
Today I get to be present for whatever this Sunday actually is.
I trust the small choices I'm making, even when no one sees them.

gratitude.prayer: I'm grateful for a Sunday I can remember. For coffee that tastes like coffee, for a body that isn't in withdrawal, for the quiet I used to be terrified of. Somewhere along the way, the boring became the beautiful, and I didn't even notice it happen.
gratitude.closing: One more day. That's the whole gift.
